coverage_notes: Phase A swept across 8 major angles: (1) market-research-report & investor-pitch conventions (meta-sources on how to structure market analysis and pitch decks); (2) value-proposition frameworks (Jobs to Be Done, Business Model Canvas, Porter's Five Forces, Blue Ocean); (3) analyst reports on adjacent categories (data visualization, low-code/no-code, graph databases, data engineering, RAG, workflow automation, BI platforms); (4) primary funding databases (Crunchbase, PitchBook, SEC EDGAR) for competitive intelligence on startups in MetroGraph's space; (5) review aggregation platforms (G2, Capterra, TrustRadius) for buyer opinion research and competitor positioning; (6) HCI & UX design research (Nielsen, Norman, Shneiderman, Tufte, Christensen) for theoretical foundations on visualization, usability, and information architecture; (7) specific competing products (Grafana, Superset, Kibana, Retool, Appsmith) with comparative analyses; (8) software architecture and implementation patterns (DDD, microservices, composable architecture, API-first design, open-source licensing models). Deduplication eliminated duplicate URLs from multiple searches. Sources tiered by: T0 = primary data/meta-analysis (SEC, Crunchbase, PitchBook, CB Insights, Gartner); T1 = peer-reviewed/analyst reports (a16z, Forrester, Straits, Grand View, IEEE, arXiv); T2 = seminal authors & textbooks (Tufte, Norman, Christensen, Shneiderman, Kim/Mauborgne); T3 = practitioner essays, blogs, guides. Parsers assigned: trafilatura for generic web content, pdf for PDFs, github-md for GitHub markdown, manpage for documentation. Notable gaps: (1) customer interview transcripts or primary user research for the graph/database visualization ICP (data engineers, noSQL startups) — Phase B/C would require primary research; (2) specific MetroGraph competitive product pages — not yet public/indexed; (3) SignalDB-specific market data — emerging technology with limited analyst coverage; (4) Angular 17 + SignalDB ecosystem maturity studies — framework combination is recent. Total: 38 high-confidence sources spanning conventions, frameworks, markets, and competitive intelligence.
